subject: Re: EdgeFin - Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@edgefin.com>, Ava Li <ava.li@edgefin.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs and benchmark next steps

Hi Sam / Ava,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to align on the use case and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a reproducible benchmark run: 

Summary of targets you mentioned:
- Latency: p95 < 150ms for short responses (~32 tokens); p95 < 350ms for long responses (~512 tokens)
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s with bursts to 400 req/s for traffic peaks
- Concurrency: average 50 concurrent requests, up to 150 during spikes
- Streaming: required for streaming token-by-token responses to the web client (chunked transfer)

Benchmark scope we propose:
1) Reproducible harness that runs both short and long prompt families, measuring cold vs warm cache, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, and sustained throughput over 5-minute windows.
2) Prompt sets: you mentioned 2 core workflows (summarization and Q&A) — if you can share the canonical prompts and a sample of real traffic (anonymized), that will help.
3) Measurement definitions: we should confirm whether you want end-to-end (client to client) latency vs server-only. Our default is server-side start-to-last-token-send; we can add client-side RTT offsets if you prefer.
4) Reproducibility: we will publish the harness, container image tags, model checkpoints, and a runbook so you can re-run.

Next steps:
- Sam, please share the prompt CSV and a small sample of request logs (anonymized) — 5k lines would be ideal but a 500-line sample is fine to start.
- Internal: I will loop in Michael to propose the harness config and timelines.
- Propose benchmark window next Tue/Wed (2027-04-05 or 2027-04-06) — does that work for you?

Attachments: none on this message.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
https://redwood.inference/docs

From: Sam Patel <sam@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Li <ava.li@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs and benchmark next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming our requirements and adding a few clarifications below.

Confirmed targets:
- p95 short responses: 150ms (end-to-end desirable, but server-side is OK to start)
- p95 long responses: 350ms
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s; acceptable to test 5-minute sustained windows
- Concurrency: tests should simulate our concurrency patterns (50 avg, spikes to 150)
- Streaming: must preserve ordered token delivery and support partial results on flush

Measurement clarifications:
- We measure latency from the time our edge client sends the request to when the last token is acknowledged by the client. For the benchmark, please provide both server-side and client-side (with synthetic network emulation) numbers.
- Cache behavior: our production workload benefits from prefix reuse, so please include warm-cache runs after a defined warm-up period (we can provide sample sequences).
- Reproducibility: provide the harness, a list of dependency versions, and the exact model checkpoint / quantization profile used.

Attached: edgefin_prompt_set_v2.csv, sample_traffic_20270329.jsonl (500 lines).

We can do your proposed run on 2027-04-05. Please share the planned test ramp and the exact time window so we can coordinate.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Platform | EdgeFin
sam@edgefin.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: michael_grant <michael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: EdgeFin - Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Michael — forwarding EdgeFin's prompt set and sample traffic. Can you review and propose a benchmark harness config that satisfies their measurement asks? Key points:
- Need server-side and client-side numbers (we can emulate client-side network characteristics)
- Warm vs cold cache runs, and a reproducible runbook (container image + checkpoint ids)
- Streaming: chunked transfers; ensure we measure end-to-end delivery ordering

Propose you share a short methodology doc and SLO matrix back to Sam, and attach the harness artifact. Targeting the 2027-04-05 window.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam@edgefin.com>, Ava Li <ava.li@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-03-31T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin - benchmark methodology proposal

Hi team,

I've reviewed the prompt set and sample traffic. Below is the proposed benchmark methodology and the definitions we'll use. I attached the harness and a draft SLO matrix.

Benchmark harness: redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.zip (contains runner, workload generator, and Dockerfile).

Measurement definitions:
- Cold latency: single request latency with an empty KV cache and no prior requests. Measured per-request server-side from receive_time to last_token_sent.
- Warm latency: measured after a defined warm-up of 10k requests that mimic prefix reuse. We will report p50/p90/p95/p99 for both cold and warm runs.
- Throughput: sustained requests per second measured over contiguous 5-minute windows. We'll report the maximum sustainable qps that maintains p95 below target.
- Concurrency: simulated by controlling the number of worker clients. Concurrency reported as simultaneous outstanding requests at test time.
- Streaming correctness: we validate ordered token delivery and measure inter-token send gaps, plus end-to-end time to first token and to last token.
- Client-side emulation: we will run a network emulation layer in the runner to add configurable RTT and throughput limits so we can approximate EdgeFin edge behaviour.

Reproducibility:
- We will publish a Docker image tag (redwood/bench:20270331-v1), the model checkpoint id, and the quantization profile used. The harness includes a seed manager to keep deterministic sampling where applicable.

Proposed test plan for 2027-04-05 (PT):
- 09:00-09:30: environment setup and smoke tests
- 09:30-10:30: cold-start latency runs (short prompts)
- 10:30-11:30: warm-cache ramp and warm latency runs
- 11:30-12:30: sustained throughput tests with concurrency profiles (50 -> 150)
- 13:00-14:00: streaming validation runs and client-side emulation
- 14:00-15:00: results collection and initial analysis

Open questions for EdgeFin:
- Please confirm if the client-side emulation parameters below match your edge: typical RTT 25ms, bandwidth 50 Mbps, and max concurrent TCP connections per client 6.
- Do you want us to include cold-start burst patterns (e.g., sudden fanout to many cold instances) in the test?

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.zip, slo_matrix.xlsx

If this looks good I can kick off a pre-run smoke test tomorrow and then schedule the main window for 2027-04-05 09:00 PT.

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael@redwoodinference.com

From: Ava Li <ava.li@edgefin.com>

Subject: Re: EdgeFin - benchmark methodology proposal

Thanks Michael — this is very thorough and matches our expectations. Confirming the client emulation params (RTT 25ms, 50 Mbps) are reasonable.

Please proceed with the smoke test tomorrow and lock 2027-04-05 09:00 PT for the main run. We are ok with you reporting both server-side and client-side numbers.

A few small asks:
- Please include the exact model checkpoint id in the report and note any non-deterministic components.
- Add a short section describing how we should interpret p99 in the context of our SLAs (is p99 a hard reject or an outlier we tolerate?).

We will make two engineers available on the run day for coordination.

Best,
Ava Li
SRE Lead | EdgeFin
